input: read ./prompt.md and follow the instructions there
task: quality fix mode: marine-detect high defect (4-connected obstacle count)

doc_friction.issue: queue flagged 7 high defects as 'changed since audit', but every flagged commit was the census commit that landed the audit itself; the check should start after the audit's own commit.

wait_for.py with --until and a log path that does not exist yet waits the full timeout for a DONE marker after the condition is met; one 9-minute wait was spent this way (pass a real log or drop the path).

deviations.why: the audit said the fix needed the dataset and the host was blocked; I probed data.vicos.si first and it answered, so I re-ran the full experiment (80 min CPU) instead of only hedging the README
deviations.did: retrained 9 runs, scored old and new rules on the same predictions
deviations.result: headline held (31.9% of 204 -> 34.6% of 80); two secondary claims withdrawn

deviations.why: the audit's medium 'tests miss core logic' defect lists model.py, which I did not test
deviations.did: left defect #3 open while covering its five named mutants

notes: Mode: fix (quality_audit.py mode; queue seed 2026-11-18-91d0). Subject research/marine-detect, audit 2026-11-17. Fixed defects 0 (high, 4-connectivity), 2 (medium, asymmetric size rule), 4 (low, missing fog interval), 6 (low, SHA never verified) via PR #17367; left 3 (model.py untested) and 7 (eWaSR uncited) open. Spot-check of the auditor: the old rule reproduced its counts exactly (204 obstacles, 80 single-pixel, 117 <=3 px). Verification: tests 18 passed (venv python, torch 2.15 CPU); 4 seeded mutants via quality_mutate.py all caught (connectivity, cover >=, MIN_AREA, ring filter); research/_homepage/build.py ok, research_live_links ok, check_md_links ok, check_posts ok, quality_audit validate 470 files 0 problems. Re-score: new rule 34.6% +- 7.2 (clean) / 35.0% +- 6.2 (aug) of 80; old rule on same predictions 31.2 / 34.0 of 204 (first run 31.9 / 33.7). Share meeting the bar: not measured in fix mode.

pricing.source: Anthropic pricing as cached in the Claude API skill (models table and per-model migration notes), 2026-10-06. Cache writes are 1.25x input (5-minute) and 2x input (1-hour); cache reads differ by model.

human_equivalent.basis: an ML researcher re-defining the metric, retraining 9 runs, rewriting results and tests

certainty.tokens: high: summed from the per-request `usage` the API returned, as the transcript recorded it, deduplicated by message id
certainty.model: high: the `model` field on each API response, not the configured model
certainty.api_equivalent_usd: medium: measured tokens x list prices in prompts/pricing.json (as_of stated); an equivalent, not a charge: these runs are billed under a subscription
certainty.time: medium: from transcript timestamps; model time is request-to-response, tool time is call-to-result, time waiting on a person is excluded from active time
certainty.human_equivalent: low: the agent's own estimate of how long a competent person would take, with its basis written down; never measured

not_counted: requests the harness makes outside the transcript (context compaction summaries, title generation, safety classifiers), if any
transcripts lost when a cloud session moved to a new container: only files present in this container are read, so a resumed session can undercount
server-tool fees (web search is billed per search, not per token); the count is recorded, not priced
CI minutes and the reviewer bots' own model calls
